title: Partial climate slopes improved 2005-2024 forecasts in three German phenology groups
abstract: We tested whether a partial climate slope can recover forecast information that a binary climate-signal gate discards. We rebuilt 11,791 series in five published data families. We fitted weights with rolling forecasts within training years to 2004 and froze them for tests from 2005 onward. The mean family median skill was 0.441 for pooled partial weights and 0.417 for a binary gate, a gain of 0.0239. A joint location and four-year block interval was 0.0136 to 0.0358. Late German plant phases and crop phases gained from weights of 0.296 and 0.389, although their full slopes reduced skill. Spring phases also gained. Crop yields and invertebrates showed little change. The result shows that rejection of a full slope does not imply absence of useful climate information. Limits include known data families, observed weather, later coverage used to select the cohort, fixed-weight uncertainty and an invertebrate weight supported by only 15 validation series. This is a retrospective method test, not a new prospective replication.

display.caption: Training weights recover useful climate information in German late plant and crop phases. Test-period optimal weights are diagnostics only.
